headline: All seven majors sit under their 200-day lines while fear reads 30, yet BTC ETF desks and Kraken whales are still pulling coin off exchanges
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it is unanimous: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE and ADA are all trading below their 200-day moving averages, and none show a golden cross. That is not a mixed market, it is a market where every major is still working from beneath its long-term trend line. Distance from the 12-month high ranges from BTC's -49% to ADA's -83%, with ETH, SOL, XRP and DOGE all sitting more than 60% off their highs. When the whole board agrees on direction like this, the story is less about any one coin and more about the structure everyone is trading inside.

Momentum tells a less uniform story than trend does, and that gap is worth naming. BTC's RSI sits at a neutral 47.4 with MACD below signal, a market resting rather than trending hard either way. ETH is the odd one out: RSI 56.3, up 1.81% over 7 days and 6.36% over 30, even though its MACD is still below signal and price remains under the 200-day. That is a momentum-versus-trend divergence, price and short-term strength improving while the longer trend line has not been reclaimed. BNB and DOGE both show MACD above signal, a mechanical bullish cross, but DOGE is still down 19.15% over 30 days, a reminder that a MACD cross is a momentum note, not a trend reversal.

Positioning is where the fragility shows up. Funding on OKX is modest for BTC (3.0% annualized) and slightly negative for ETH (-0.7%), meaning ETH shorts are the ones paying to hold their bet, a small tilt against the bears. SOL, XRP and DOGE tell a different story: funding annualizes to 9.3%, 5.6% and 11.0% respectively, with long/short account ratios of 2.15, 3.68 and 4.65. That is a crowd stacked long and paying for the privilege. The last 24 hours of liquidations lean hard against those longs holding up: SOL saw $2.29M in short liquidations against just $63,630 in longs, and BTC saw $381,917 in short liquidations against $1,285 in longs, both windows where short positions, not longs, took the bulk of the forced exits.

On flows, the BTC spot ETF printed a net $101.7M on 07 Aug 2026, and the five-session net is +$865.3M with all five days pointing the same direction, so the inflow run has persisted through the window given. ETH ETF flows were positive too, +$49.6M on the same day and +$243.7M over five sessions, but only 4 of those days share the same direction, so call it a strong stretch rather than an unbroken streak. Stablecoin float, the market's dry powder, sits at $306.2B and is down 0.75% over 30 days, a mild contraction rather than a buildup. Whale activity adds another data point: $168.1M in BTC moved off exchanges in the last 24 hours, including two Kraken withdrawals of $117.99M and $50.07M, and the last four days of weekly net flow read -$279.9M, +$380.9M, +$1,273.2M, +$132.2M, net positive across that stretch with three of four days showing coin leaving exchanges.

Set against all that, the Fear & Greed Index reads 30, labeled Fear, sitting near the top of its own 30-day range of 22 to 33. So the crowd's mood is fearful while the ETF tape has bought BTC net-positive for five straight sessions and whale wallets have been pulling coin into custody rather than staging it near exchanges. That is the day's central tension: sentiment says fear, the flow data says accumulation. Total market cap is basically flat, up 0.69% over 24 hours to $2.303T, and BTC dominance holds at 56.6%, so none of this has yet reshuffled the balance between BTC and the rest of the field.

Worth watching from here: whether BTC's ETF same_direction_days streak breaks or extends beyond five, whether the crowded long positioning in SOL, XRP and DOGE (funding above 9% annualized, long/short ratios above 2) resolves through a funding flip, and whether any major reclaims its 200-day line, which none currently hold. A reversal in the stablecoin float's 30-day decline, or a shift in whale flow back toward exchanges after four days of net outflow-leaning activity, would also change the shape of this read.
